records.source: Τὸ λοιπὸν προσεύχεσθε, ἀδελφοί, περὶ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ὁ λόγος τοῦ κυρίου τρέχῃ καὶ δοξάζηται καθὼς καὶ πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἵνα ῥυσθῶμεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀτόπων καὶ πονηρῶν ἀνθρώπων, οὐ γὰρ πάντων ἡ πίστις.
records.gloss: Finally pray, brothers, for us, that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, just as also with you, \v 2 and that we may be rescued from the perverse and evil men, for not of all [is] the faith.
pieces: Finally, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, pray for us: pray that the word of the Lord may run swiftly and be glorified everywhere, as it was among you,
and that we may be rescued from perverse and wicked people, for faith is not found in everyone.

L.1: Finally, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, just as [it was] also with you,
L.2: and that we may be delivered from perverse and evil {{gender:people|men}}, for not all [have] faith.

R.1: And now, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, pray for us. Pray that the Lord's message will spread quickly and be given glory everywhere, as it was among you.
R.2: Pray also that we will be rescued from bad and evil people, because not everyone has faith.

decisions.choice: finally: as for the rest
decisions.reason: λοιπὸν, as in 1 Thessalonians 4:1, turns to the closing section.

decisions.choice: may run and be glorified: spread swiftly and be honored
decisions.reason: The word of the Lord is pictured as a runner (Psalm 147:15, "his word runs swiftly"). It is glorified when people receive it as God's word, as the Thessalonians did (1 Thessalonians 2:13).

decisions.choice: perverse and evil people: particular opponents where Paul is
decisions.reason: The article points to known opponents, probably in Corinth (Acts 18:5-17).

decisions.choice: not all have faith
decisions.reason: πάντων ἡ πίστις means faith is not held by all people: not everyone believes, so the gospel meets opposition. The article may also mean "the faith", but the sense is the same. It sets up a play on words in verse 3: people may be faithless, but the Lord is faithful.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general; Balanced and Readable say "people".

decisions.choice: will spread quickly and be given glory
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the runner (m2) and keeps the key term "glory".

records.heading: Pray for us

records.source: πιστὸς δέ ἐστιν ὁ κύριος, ὃς στηρίξει ὑμᾶς καὶ φυλάξει ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
records.gloss: Faithful but is the Lord, who will strengthen you and guard from the evil [one].
pieces: But the Lord can be trusted: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make you strong and guard you from the evil one.

L.3: But the Lord is faithful, who will strengthen you and guard [you] from the evil one.

R.3: But the Lord is faithful. He will make you strong and keep you safe from the evil one.

decisions.choice: the evil one: Satan
decisions.reason: πονηροῦ can be masculine ("the evil one") or neuter ("evil"). The source data takes it as masculine, and Paul has spoken of Satan's work in 2:9; Jesus' prayer "deliver us from the evil one" (Matthew 6:13) has the same ambiguity.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the Lord is faithful"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "God". The meaning is close (1 Thessalonians 5:24).

decisions.choice: faithful: in contrast to faithless people
decisions.reason: πιστὸς picks up "faith" in verse 2: even where people are faithless, the Lord is faithful.

records.source: πεποίθαμεν δὲ ἐν κυρίῳ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, ὅτι ἃ παραγγέλλομεν καὶ ποιεῖτε καὶ ποιήσετε.
records.gloss: We are confident now in [the] Lord about you, that what we command both you are doing and will do.
pieces: Because of the Lord, we are confident about you: you are doing what we tell you, and you will go on doing it.

L.4: And we are confident in [the] Lord about you, that you are doing and will do the things we command.

R.4: The Lord gives us confidence that you are obeying our teaching, and that you will keep on obeying it.

decisions.choice: confident in the Lord about you: our trust rests on the Lord, not only on you
decisions.reason: Paul's confidence about them comes from his confidence in the Lord who strengthens them (verse 3).

decisions.choice: what we command: preparing for the commands of verses 6-15
decisions.reason: παραγγέλλω is the word for giving orders; it returns in verses 6, 10 and 12.

records.source: ὁ δὲ κύριος κατευθύναι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας εἰς τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ εἰς τὴν ὑπομονὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: The now Lord may direct your hearts into the love of the God and into the endurance of the Christ.
pieces: May the Lord guide your hearts into the love of God and the endurance of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.5: And may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the endurance of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.5: We pray that the Lord will help you understand more and more how much God loves you, and help you keep going with patience, as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} did.

decisions.choice: the love of God and the endurance of Christ: God's love for them, and the endurance Christ showed and gives
alternatives: their love for God and their patient waiting for Christ
decisions.reason: Both genitives can be read either way: God's love for them or theirs for God; Christ's own endurance or their patient waiting for him. Paul most likely means that they are drawn deeper into God's love for them and share the steadfastness Christ showed in suffering.

decisions.choice: direct your hearts: make a straight way for them
decisions.reason: κατευθύνω is the verb of 1 Thessalonians 3:11, "direct our way".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}".

decisions.choice: understand more and more how much God loves you; keep going with patience, as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} did
alternatives: into the love of God and into the endurance of Christ
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m1, which is uncertain.

records.source: Παραγγέλλομεν δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, ἐν ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ στέλλεσθαι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἀδελφοῦ ἀτάκτως περιπατοῦντος καὶ μὴ κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ἣν παρελάβοσαν παρ’ ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: We command now you, brothers, in [the] name of the Lord of us Jesus Christ to keep away you from every brother disorderly walking and not according to the tradition which they received from us.
pieces: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, in the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} we command you: keep your distance from any {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} who lives an undisciplined life, contrary to the tradition they received from us.

L.6: Now we command you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, in [the] name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, to keep away from every {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} who walks in a disorderly way and not according to the tradition that they received from us.

R.6: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we give you this command with the authority of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}: stay away from any believer who refuses to work and does not live the way we taught.

decisions.choice: disorderly: out of line, here refusing to work
decisions.reason: ἀτάκτως is the adverb of the word in 1 Thessalonians 5:14, used of soldiers out of rank or of failing to show up for work. Verses 7-12 make the meaning plain here: some members had stopped working and were living off others.

decisions.choice: keep away from: draw back from close fellowship
decisions.reason: στέλλομαι means to hold oneself aloof, to avoid. It is not expelling them as enemies (verse 15) but refusing to support their way of life.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "they received"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "you received". The SBLGNT reads the plural "they", referring to the disorderly members. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the tradition: Paul's teaching, here about work
decisions.reason: As in 2:15, the teaching handed on, including the instruction about work of verse 10.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}
decisions.reason: Any member, man or woman; "brother" is the traditional form. Readable says "believer".

decisions.choice: refuses to work
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense the context gives (m1).

records.heading: Anyone who will not work

records.source: αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε πῶς δεῖ μιμεῖσθαι ἡμᾶς, ὅτι οὐκ ἠτακτήσαμεν ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδὲ δωρεὰν ἄρτον ἐφάγομεν παρά τινος, ἀλλ’ ἐν κόπῳ καὶ μόχθῳ νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐργαζόμενοι πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐπιβαρῆσαί τινα ὑμῶν·
records.gloss: Yourselves for you know how it is necessary to imitate us, because not we were disorderly among you \v 8 nor freely bread we ate from anyone, but in labor and toil night and day working so as not to burden any of you;
pieces: You know yourselves that you should imitate us. We did not live idly among you,
and we never ate anyone's bread as a gift; we labored and toiled, working night and day, so as not to be a burden to any of you.

L.7: For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not disorderly among you,
L.8: nor did we eat bread from anyone without paying, but with labor and toil, working night and day, so as not to be a burden to any of you.

R.7: You know that you should live the way we lived. We were not lazy when we were with you.
R.8: We did not eat anyone's food without paying for it. We worked hard day and night, so that we would not be a burden to any of you.

decisions.choice: we were not disorderly: we did not shirk work
decisions.reason: ἀτακτέω is the verb of the word in verse 6.

decisions.choice: eat bread freely: live at someone else's expense
decisions.reason: "To eat bread" means to earn one's living (Genesis 3:19); "freely" means without paying.

decisions.choice: labor and toil, night and day
decisions.reason: The same words as 1 Thessalonians 2:9: Paul supported himself by his trade (Acts 18:3).

decisions.choice: live idly (B); lazy (R)
decisions.reason: Here the context makes the sense of "disorderly" plain (verse 6, m1).

records.source: οὐχ ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν, ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἑαυτοὺς τύπον δῶμεν ὑμῖν εἰς τὸ μιμεῖσθαι ἡμᾶς.
records.gloss: not that not we have right, but so that ourselves [as] an example we might give to you so as to imitate us.
pieces: It was not that we had no right to support, but we wanted to give you an example to follow.

L.9: Not that we do not have the right, but so that we might give ourselves to you as an example to imitate.

R.9: We had the right to ask you for help, but we did not do it. We wanted to show you how to live, so that you would live the same way.

decisions.choice: the right: the right to be supported by those they served
decisions.reason: Paul argues for this right at length in 1 Corinthians 9:4-14, and gives it up for the sake of the gospel.

decisions.choice: the right to support
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the right was (m1).

records.source: καὶ γὰρ ὅτε ἦμεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, τοῦτο παρηγγέλλομεν ὑμῖν, ὅτι εἴ τις οὐ θέλει ἐργάζεσθαι μηδὲ ἐσθιέτω.
records.gloss: And indeed when we were with you, this we were commanding you, that if anyone not is willing to work, neither let him eat.
pieces: For even while we were with you, we gave you this instruction: "Anyone who will not work should not eat."

L.10: For even when we were with you, we kept giving you this command: "If anyone is not willing to work, neither should [that person] eat."

R.10: When we were with you, we gave you this rule: "If someone does not want to work, they should not eat."

decisions.choice: if anyone is not willing to work: refusing, not unable
decisions.reason: θέλει ("is willing") makes it a matter of refusal. Those who cannot work are not in view; the church cared for those in need (1 Timothy 5:3-16).

decisions.choice: we kept commanding: a rule given more than once
decisions.reason: The imperfect παρηγγέλλομεν suggests a saying Paul repeated, perhaps already a familiar rule.

records.source: ἀκούομεν γάρ τινας περιπατοῦντας ἐν ὑμῖν ἀτάκτως, μηδὲν ἐργαζομένους ἀλλὰ περιεργαζομένους·
records.gloss: We hear for some walking among you disorderly, nothing working but working around;
pieces: We hear that some among you are living undisciplined lives: they are not busy working, they are busy with everyone else's business.

L.11: For we hear that some are walking among you in a disorderly way, not working at all but being busybodies.

R.11: We hear that some people among you are not working. Instead, they are getting into other people's business.

decisions.choice: not working but working around: a play on words
decisions.reason: ἐργάζομαι is to work; περιεργάζομαι is to fuss about, to meddle. Not busy, but busybodies.

decisions.choice: they are not busy working, they are busy with everyone else's business
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the play on words (m1).

records.source: τοῖς δὲ τοιούτοις παραγγέλλομεν καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν ἐν κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ ἵνα μετὰ ἡσυχίας ἐργαζόμενοι τὸν ἑαυτῶν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν.
records.gloss: To the now such we command and urge in [the] Lord Jesus Christ that with quietness working their own bread they eat.
pieces: We command such people, and we urge them in the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, to go about their work quietly and to eat bread they have earned themselves.

L.12: Now we command and urge such people in [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} that they work quietly and eat their own bread.

R.12: In the name of the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, we tell these people, and we beg them, to settle down, work quietly and earn their own food.

decisions.choice: quietness: a settled, orderly life
decisions.reason: ἡσυχίας is the quiet life of 1 Thessalonians 4:11, the opposite of meddling (verse 11).

decisions.choice: eat their own bread: live on what they earn
decisions.reason: The bread is "their own", not someone else's (verse 8).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

records.source: ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί, μὴ ἐγκακήσητε καλοποιοῦντες.
records.gloss: You but, brothers, not grow weary doing good.
pieces: As for you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, do not lose heart in doing what is right.

L.13: But you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, do not grow weary in doing good.

R.13: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, never get tired of doing what is good.

decisions.choice: do not grow weary in doing good: even when some take advantage
decisions.reason: The faithful members might be tempted to stop helping others because some were abusing their generosity. Paul tells them not to give up (Galatians 6:9).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

records.source: Εἰ δέ τις οὐχ ὑπακούει τῷ λόγῳ ἡμῶν διὰ τῆς ἐπιστολῆς, τοῦτον σημειοῦσθε, μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι αὐτῷ, ἵνα ἐντραπῇ·
records.gloss: If now anyone not obeys the word of us through the letter, this [one] take note of, not to associate with him, so that he may be ashamed;
pieces: If anyone will not obey what we say in this letter, take note of that person and have nothing to do with them, so that they will be ashamed.

L.14: And if anyone does not obey our word through this letter, take note of that person and do not associate with [that one], so that [the person] may be put to shame.

R.14: Some people may not obey what we tell you in this letter. Notice who they are, and do not spend time with them. Then they will feel ashamed.

decisions.choice: take note and do not associate: mark them, and keep apart from them
decisions.reason: σημειόομαι is to mark or note. συναναμίγνυμι is to mix with, keep company with (1 Corinthians 5:9-11).

decisions.choice: so that they may be ashamed: the aim is to bring them to their senses
decisions.reason: ἐντρέπω is to be made ashamed, to be turned back by shame. The discipline aims at restoration (verse 15).

decisions.choice: that person ... [that one] ... [the person]
decisions.reason: The Greek "anyone" may be a man or a woman; Literal avoids "him" (as Balanced and Readable do).

records.source: καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐχθρὸν ἡγεῖσθε, ἀλλὰ νουθετεῖτε ὡς ἀδελφόν.
records.gloss: and not as an enemy regard [him], but admonish as a brother.
pieces: But do not treat that person as an enemy; correct them as a {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}.

L.15: And do not regard [that person] as an enemy, but admonish [that person] as a {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}.

R.15: But do not treat them like an enemy. Warn them as you would warn a fellow believer.

decisions.choice: not as an enemy, but as a brother: still family
decisions.reason: Keeping apart is not cutting off. They are still to be warned as members of God's family (1 Thessalonians 5:14).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}
decisions.reason: Any member, man or woman; "brother" is the traditional form. Readable says "fellow believer".

records.source: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ κύριος τῆς εἰρήνης δῴη ὑμῖν τὴν εἰρήνην διὰ παντὸς ἐν παντὶ τρόπῳ.
records.gloss: Himself now the Lord of the peace may give you the peace through all in every way.
pieces: Now may the Lord of peace {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} grant you peace continually and in every way.

L.16: Now may the Lord of peace {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} give you peace always, in every way.

R.16: We pray that the Lord, who gives peace, will give you peace at all times and in every situation.

decisions.choice: the Lord of peace: the Lord Jesus, who gives peace
decisions.reason: In 1 Thessalonians 5:23 it is "the God of peace"; here the same is said of the Lord Jesus.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in every way"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "place" for "way"; the words differ by one letter in Greek.

decisions.choice: the Lord, who gives peace
decisions.reason: Readable says what "Lord of peace" means (m1).

records.heading: Peace, and Paul's own greeting

records.gloss: The Lord [be] with all of you.
pieces: The Lord be with you all.

L.16: The Lord [be] with all of you.

R.16: May the Lord be with all of you.

decisions.choice: with all of you: including the disorderly
decisions.reason: πάντων ὑμῶν ("all of you") comes three times at the end of the letter (verses 16 and 18).

records.source: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου, ὅ ἐστιν σημεῖον ἐν πάσῃ ἐπιστολῇ· οὕτως γράφω.
records.gloss: The greeting with the my hand of Paul, which is [a] sign in every letter; so I write.
pieces: This greeting is in my own handwriting, Paul's. It is the sign of genuineness in every letter; this is how I write.

L.17: The greeting [is] in my own hand, Paul's, which is a sign in every letter; this is how I write.

R.17: I, Paul, am writing this greeting with my own hand. I do this in every letter as a sign that the letter really comes from me. This is how I write.

decisions.choice: the greeting in my own hand: a sign that the letter is genuine
decisions.reason: Paul dictated his letters and wrote the closing himself (1 Corinthians 16:21; Colossians 4:18). Here he points to it as a mark of a genuine letter, perhaps because a letter "as if from us" had caused trouble (2:2).

decisions.choice: sign: a mark that shows something is genuine
decisions.reason: σημεῖον here is a token or mark of identity, not a miracle.

records.source: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: The grace of the Lord of us Jesus Christ [be] with all of you.
pieces: May the grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} be with you all.

L.18: The grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [be] with all of you.

R.18: May the grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} be with all of you.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen" at the end
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Amen", as copyists often did at the end of a book.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.
